title: Half-Mast
subject: a fourteen-year-old who grew three inches over the summer holidays and turns up on the first day of the new school year in last year's trousers, two inches above his socks, and decides to strut it out
caption: 70s glam rock stomp revival. Fuzzed-out Les Paul riff with a chugging boogie rhythm, stomping kick and floor tom on every beat, big handclaps, pounding honky-tonk piano, honking baritone saxophone stabs. Loud saturated 70s mix with room-heavy drums. Male lead in a raspy chest voice with a sneer, gang-shout backing vocals on the hooks. 128 BPM, E major. Cocky, loud and laughing. No pop-punk, no autotune, no trap, no synth-pop, no metal screaming.
lyrics:
[Intro - stomp, claps and fuzz riff]

[Verse 1]
Went to bed in June a shrimp
Woke up taller than my mum
September came, the trousers didn't
Socks out for everyone

[Chorus]
Half-mast, half-mast
Ankles in the open air
Half-mast, half-mast
Walk like you don't care

[Verse 2]
Mr Price looked at my shins
Said is there a flood today
I said sir, these are a statement
And the whole class clapped away

[Chorus]
Half-mast, half-mast
Stripy socks on show
Half-mast, half-mast
Strut it, there you go

[Bridge - sax solo, then gang shouts]
Mum's got the needle out tonight
Let it down an inch or two

[Chorus]
Half-mast, half-mast
Kids all doing it too
Half-mast, half-mast
Whole school's in on it now

[Outro - stomp and claps]
Half-mast
Take a bow
